papers.summary: This study examines the evolution of the Aegean Robotics Competition (ARC) from a face-to-face educational robotics event to an online competition format. Using a longitudinal case study approach, participation records and questionnaire data collected from students, coaches, organizers, and judges across five competition cycles (2017–2022) were analyzed. papers.summary: This dissertation examines the history of the auxiliaires de l'Apostolat, Catholic laywomen who are called by their bishop to support him in his apostolate through societal presence and spiritual exercise. papers.title: Spaced repetition and list-strength in recognition memory
papers.summary: Intuition and classic mathematical models suggest that "strong" list items should see a competitive recognition-memory advantage when mixed with "weak" list items within a single list. This holds for manipulations of reading aloud but not other manipulations. Study time per item (e.g., 500 vs. 2000 ms), can even invert the effect, with a larger strength effect between pure-strength lists than within mixed lists. papers.title: ARC — Reflexive Architecture of Consciousness: Dissolving the Hard Problem through Architectural Identity
papers.summary: Abstract: The hard problem of consciousness asks why there is something it is like to be a physical system. This paper presents the Reflexive Architecture of Consciousness (ARC), a formal theory that dissolves the hard problem by showing that the question that sustains it arises from an incomplete description. The theory's central claim is the Principle of Architectural Identity (PAI): the quale Q is identical to the reflexive functioning of an embodied architecture A, expressed as Q = f(A). papers.title: Gossip, Slander and Accusation in Hittite Society
papers.summary: In Hittite society, oral communication was a powerful dynamic influencing daily interaction, political structure, and divine order. papers.title: Intelligent Threat Detection in Cloud Environments: Integrating Machine Learning with Blockchain for Enhanced Digital Security
papers.summary: This paper presents an intelligent threat detection framework for cloud environments by integrating machine learning techniques with blockchain technology to enhance digital security and data integrity. With the rapid adoption of cloud computing, enterprises and users face major concerns from security threats and data breaches. Traditional security mechanisms often fail to provide real-time, tamper-proof threat detection in dynamic cloud environments. Several studies use machine learning models for intrusion detection; however, they face data manipulation risks and centralized vulnerabilities.
